Each is reduced from the raw draw dict the run already executes (raw["random_matched"] / raw["random"], net_return reshaped to (draws, attempts)): the mean over the draws whose net_return is finite, i.e. the scored controls (execution.execute sets net_return to NaN for every unscored status). Study itself instantiates fine on a synthetic panel with the E1 family (verified).

idx-signals/idxsig/e5.py (new, not mine): Stage 1/2 must score discovery-fitted coefficients before the literals are frozen; the module exposes score(), flags(), detector_states(), rank_features()/features() for that, but a registered E5_CAND_<MARKET>_<ARM> rule refuses to compute until the literals are committed, so Stage-2 harness runs need either the freeze first (as the draft's stage 3 says) or an e5.py-built Rule carrying the discovery coefficients.

research/E5/protocol.json (freeze, not mine): should state the module's concrete choices listed under open_concerns (rank formula, vol20 variant, vc10_60 min_periods, rebase pre/peak, IDX spike union, NaN-counts-as-outside debounce, one FEATURE_ORDER for all markets).
open_concerns: IDX spike for `rebase`: implemented as (ret1 >= 0.30) | (lock_up & tradeable), identical to the draft on US/CRYPTO (lock_up is all False there) but on IDX a superset of the draft's 'lock_up & tradeable' (it also counts a literal +30% close in the sub-Rp200 band, where 35% limits allow one). A rule cannot know its market, so a market-agnostic definition was needed; the protocol should either adopt this union or specify how the IDX form is selected.

vol20 follows e1.Study._signals (present-but-untraded session = 0 log return), not moonshot_g.features (such sessions dropped); the two differ only on IDX names with untraded sessions. The quiet band and vc10_60 use the same series. Chosen because the E1/E2 signal_stats tables were computed from Study._signals.
vc10_60 min_periods (8 of 10, 45 of 60) are my choice (vol20's 15/20 ratio); the draft does not specify them.

rebase: pre = level(s0-1), peak = max level(s0..t), 'exists any s0 in [t-40, t-6]'; the draft names the three conditions but not pre/peak explicitly. A missing (non-present) session anywhere in s0-1..t makes the test fail for that s0 (np.maximum propagates NaN).

creep5v20 requires full windows (5 and 20 present sessions); a name with a presence gap in t-24..t has NaN creep (rank 0.5, A0 False). price_facts.py instead drops bars with missing fields and re-indexes; identical on gap-free series (tested), different across gaps.

Debounce convention: a NaN score (warm-up, not evaluable) counts as 'outside' the top set, and nothing flags before 5 sessions of history; so columns 60..64 of a view can flag. Every harness window starts 60 sessions before its period, so this never touches a period session; stated here because the draft's 'outside it' wording could also be read as 'five evaluable sessions below'.
Percentile rank formula (rank - 0.5)/n with average ties (midrank; a single-name pool ranks 0.5); the draft says 'percentile rank' without the formula. Ranks fall in (0, 1), not [0, 1].

One FEATURE_ORDER (41 columns) for all markets: gap on IDX ranks 0.5 everywhere and ara off IDX is 0 everywhere, constant columns the e5.py fit must tolerate (L2 ridge keeps them finite); alternatively e5.py could zero their coefficients.

The candidate rule for an unfrozen arm raises rather than returning all-False (deliberate: no silent zero-signal harness run); family_flags() returns all-False for it so e1.Study and paper-style feature tables still build. Both behaviours are tested.

Rule hash: the per-market literals are inside the module source, so freezing them (stage 3) changes every E5 rule's sha, including A0/A1's, which is the intended 'rule hash covers them' but means A0/A1 discovery-stage runs recorded before the freeze will carry a different sha than post-freeze runs.
